views.name: Context and trust boundaries
views.view_type: context block view (flowchart LR with nested boundaries)
views.question: What is inside the system boundary, which external actors and systems does it touch, and where are the trust boundaries?
views.concern: Scope boundary, hosting on shared resources (one Fire TV stick, one AWS account), secret handling, untrusted input, launch safety.
views.rationale: A boundary view is the cheapest way to fix system scope and the four trust boundaries before requirements are allocated.
views.abstraction: Component level; protocols named only at trust boundaries. Omits data schemas, deployment sizing, CI.
views.interpretation: tv-app/ and backend/ are the system. TB1 HTTPS with per-device bearer token; TB2 Yahoo tokens and client secret server-side only (SSM SecureString); TB3 ESPN responses untrusted and validated at ingest; TB4 provider launch by explicit intent to allow-listed packages. Alexa is optional (C8).
views.supported_decision: Requirement allocation per component and trust boundary; interface requirements for TB1..TB4.
views.limitations: Planned design from the Planning and Design node; nothing is realized. Explanatory Mermaid plus hand-written SVG; not a SysML v2 model (sysml_claim false). Requirement mappings are not final until the Requirements Engineer passes. Provider app is a placeholder until spike SP-3 picks one.
views.canonical_source: views/v1-context.mmd (explanatory); design authority stays with the Planning and Design artifacts and journey.json decisions

views.name: Use cases and outcomes
views.view_type: use-case view (hand-drawn UML-style in SVG; stadium nodes in Mermaid)
views.question: Which customer goals does the product serve for retained items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and the right-side panel, and what observable outcome ends each?
views.concern: Customer-visible behaviour and honesty constraints (installed is not subscribed; red zone is team context; unknown access stays unknown; GAME_OPENED only from device observation).
views.rationale: Outcome boxes give the Requirements Engineer and Test Engineer a verifiable end state per use case.
views.abstraction: Goal level; no screens or API calls. Omits item 5 (not retained) and messaging (excluded).
views.interpretation: UC-3 extends to UC-4 through the Watch action. Panel outcome differs only in the video source: provider video (Mode B) or labeled sample footage (Mode A).
views.supported_decision: Functional requirement set and acceptance outcomes per retained item.
views.limitations: Planned design from the Planning and Design node; nothing is realized. Explanatory Mermaid plus hand-written SVG; not a SysML v2 model (sysml_claim false). Requirement mappings are not final until the Requirements Engineer passes. Mermaid has no native use-case diagram; the .mmd uses stadium nodes for the same content.
views.canonical_source: views/v2-use-cases.mmd (explanatory); design authority stays with the Planning and Design artifacts and journey.json decisions

views.name: Operational flow
views.question: How does a live game event become a heads-up alert and a provider launch, how does the panel refresh, and where does Mode B fall back to Mode A?
views.concern: End-to-end behaviour, fallbacks (C2 replay, C5 Mode A, C6 manual lineup), suppression and correction handling, launch outcome truthfulness.
views.rationale: The alert path crosses both systems and three trust boundaries; a flow view exposes every decision a requirement must cover.
views.abstraction: Step level; no timing values beyond spike_panel_max; long-poll and refresh intervals are unset.
views.interpretation: ESPN poll -> validate (else labeled replay) -> normalize/dedupe/corrections -> match against starters -> policy -> /v1/alerts long-poll -> heads-up notification -> Watch -> resolver -> explicit intent -> typed launch outcome. Panel path GET /v1/panel -> PanelService -> render with stale marks. SP-4 verdict picks Mode B or Mode A.
views.supported_decision: Behavioural requirements, fault behaviour, and V&V scenarios (replay, suppression, each launch outcome, each panel mode).
views.limitations: Planned design from the Planning and Design node; nothing is realized. Explanatory Mermaid plus hand-written SVG; not a SysML v2 model (sysml_claim false). Requirement mappings are not final until the Requirements Engineer passes. No timing budgets (owner: lightweight design, no benchmarks).
views.canonical_source: views/v3-operational-flow.mmd (explanatory); design authority stays with the Planning and Design artifacts and journey.json decisions

views.name: Delivery tooling flow
views.view_type: process flow (flowchart TB) with artifact-derivation lane
views.question: How do every entry point reach one gate, when does vnv-review run, and how does the shared spec-authoring skill reach this repo's spec gate and the D1 build?
views.concern: One verdict for local, CI and harness runs; workflow safety (C14); vnv typed gap (C12); hook ordering (C13); private-to-public vendoring of D5; rule 12 hygiene.
views.rationale: D4 and D5 are tooling deliverables with many entry points and one shared resource (Alphazedehq skills/ tree); a flow view shows the single gate and the vendoring seam.
views.abstraction: Artifact and step level; no per-harness hook mechanics (deferred to Planning and Design); no workflow YAML.
views.interpretation: Git hooks, Actions and harness hooks (via Alphazedehq:hooks/ci-gate-hook.sh) all call tools/ci/gate.sh AREA (android, backend, spec, hygiene). ship-pull-request runs vnv-review when a guidance tree exists, else REFUSED_NO_VNV (never a pass). D5 generalizes the GridMarket kit into Alphazedehq:skills/spec-authoring/, vendors scripts to tools/spec/, and the spec area lints and builds D1. SD-013 (copy GridMarket kit) is superseded and not shown.
views.supported_decision: D4/D5 file layout, lane order (C13), and the spec gate area contents.
views.limitations: Planned design from the Planning and Design node; nothing is realized. Explanatory Mermaid plus hand-written SVG; not a SysML v2 model (sysml_claim false). Requirement mappings are not final until the Requirements Engineer passes. REFUSED_NO_VNV terminal does not model whether merge proceeds in repos without a guidance tree (not decided). vnv-review also accepts Vnv/AGENTS.md (Alphazedehq:skills/vnv-review/SKILL.md:20-21).
views.canonical_source: views/v4-delivery-tooling.mmd (explanatory); design authority stays with the Planning and Design artifacts and journey.json decisions
